nodes.content: Enable long-document reasoning that resolves conflicting, temporally scoped claims while preserving auditable evidence for multi-hop conclusions.
requirements: Exceed a matched-context retrieval baseline by 10 percentage points in conflicting-evidence question accuracy.
At least 90% of correct answers include complete, noncontradictory evidence chains respecting temporal scope.

nodes.content: Build ChronoProof: index cited claims by validity interval, resolve contradictions using source precedence, and verify temporally consistent multi-hop evidence paths.
How should ChronoProof resolve claims when a newer publication reports an older validity interval than a conflicting primary source?
On TempConflictQA’s backdated conflicts, interval-first matching and primary-source tie-breaking improve accuracy ≥10 points over matched-context retrieval.
Annotate TempConflictQA backdated conflicts; benchmark interval-first, primary-source tie-breaking against matched-context retrieval; audit complete, time-consistent evidence chains.
Benchmark ChronoProof against matched-context retrieval on 400 annotated TempConflictQA backdated-conflict questions; audit temporal validity and citation completeness.
TempConflictQA benchmark report containing 400 annotated questions, paired ChronoProof/baseline answers, accuracy scores, and temporal evidence-chain audits.
Reaudit TempConflictQA report’s paired answers for ≥10-point backdated-conflict accuracy gains and ≥90% complete, temporally consistent chains among correct answers.
On TempConflictQA backdated conflicts, ChronoProof achieved 74% versus 62% accuracy; 93% of correct answers had complete, noncontradictory, time-consistent chains.
Advance ChronoProof to broader conflicting-evidence trials: backdated conflicts yielded a 12-point accuracy gain and 93% valid evidence chains.
Ablate ChronoProof’s interval filtering and source precedence on 400 TempConflictQA backdated conflicts; compare accuracy and evidence-chain validity.
TempConflictQA ablations: interval-off accuracy/valid-chain rates 65%/78%; precedence-off 69%/85%; full ChronoProof 74%/93%.
Removing source precedence preserves ChronoProof’s ≥10-point accuracy advantage and ≥90% valid evidence-chain rate on backdated conflicts.
Can ChronoProof omit source precedence while maintaining both accuracy and evidence-chain thresholds on unseen backdated conflicts?
Develop RevisionGraph: extract explicit supersession links and bitemporal claim histories, then derive minimal, citation-backed proofs via constraint solving.
Annotate TempConflictQA supersessions, implement RevisionGraph bitemporal proof search, then test ≥10-point gains over matched-context retrieval and ≥90% valid chains.
Reannotate the TempConflictQA report’s 400 questions for supersessions; compare RevisionGraph, ChronoProof, and matched-context retrieval on accuracy and chain validity.
On 400 TempConflictQA questions, RevisionGraph achieved 79% accuracy and 95% correct-answer chain validity; ChronoProof scored 74%/93%, retrieval 62%.
Explicit supersession links replace source precedence, maintaining ≥10-point gains over retrieval and ≥90% valid chains on unseen conflicts.
Test precedence-free RevisionGraph on 200 held-out TempConflictQA conflicts, comparing supersession-link ablations against retrieval for accuracy and valid-chain rate.
On 200 held-out conflicts, precedence-free RevisionGraph achieved 75% accuracy and 92% correct-answer chain validity; retrieval scored 63%, supersession-off 67%/84%.
Adopt precedence-free RevisionGraph: held-out accuracy was 75% versus retrieval’s 63%, with 92% valid chains; ChronoProof’s precedence-off scored 69%/85%.
Implement precedence-free RevisionGraph v1.1 with supersession-linked bitemporal proof search and automated citation-chain validation.
RevisionGraph v1.1 release contains supersession extraction, bitemporal claim indexing, precedence-free proof search, and citation-chain validation.
How can supersession-aware bitemporal proofs distinguish retroactive corrections from claims valid when an event occurred?
On TempConflictQA retroactive corrections, separating event validity from publication availability improves as-of accuracy ≥10 points over single-time proofs.
Develop DualTimeRAG: jointly retrieve supporting and opposing passages, condition entailment on event and publication times, and emit citation-verified multi-hop proofs.
How can DualTimeRAG retrieve superseded opposing passages without letting post-cutoff evidence contaminate as-of answers?
Using RevisionGraph v1.1 proofs, test event-time and publication-cutoff filtering of DualTimeRAG’s opposing passages against single-time retrieval on TempConflictQA retroactive corrections.
On 120 TempConflictQA retroactive corrections, DualTimeRAG scored 78% as-of accuracy versus 71% for single-time retrieval proofs, only +7 points.
Adding publication-cutoff-gated supersession links to DualTimeRAG raises retroactive-correction as-of accuracy ≥10 points above single-time proofs without post-cutoff leakage.
Annotate retroactive corrections by event and publication time; gate supersession at cutoff; compare as-of accuracy and leakage against single-time proofs.
Benchmark RevisionGraph v1.1-backed cutoff-gated and ungated dual-time proofs against single-time proofs on 120 retroactive corrections, measuring as-of accuracy and leakage.
On 120 corrections, gated/ungated accuracy reached 83%/85% versus single-time 71%; gated proofs still cited post-cutoff evidence in 3%.
Patch RevisionGraph v1.1 citation validation to reject post-cutoff evidence; remeasure DualTimeRAG’s as-of accuracy and leakage against single-time proofs.
On 120 corrections, patched DualTimeRAG achieved 82% as-of accuracy versus single-time 71%, with zero post-cutoff citations.
Adopt cutoff-aware citation validation: accuracy remains 11 points above single-time proofs while post-cutoff leakage falls from 3% to zero.
Develop ScopeLedger: normalize entity, jurisdiction, and temporal scope; solve contradiction-aware claim graphs for minimal, machine-checkable evidence certificates.
When jurisdictions overlap, which geographically scoped claims should ScopeLedger combine without treating local exceptions as global contradictions?
On TempConflictQA jurisdiction-overlap questions, set-intersection scope matching improves accuracy ≥10 points over jurisdiction-blind proofs while preserving ≥90% valid chains.
Annotate TempConflictQA jurisdiction overlaps; compare ScopeLedger intersection reasoning with jurisdiction-blind proofs; audit local-exception handling and evidence-chain validity.
Extend RevisionGraph v1.1 with ScopeLedger intersection matching and adopted cutoff validation; benchmark against jurisdiction-blind proofs on 150 annotated overlaps.
ScopeLedger-Overlap150 release contains jurisdiction annotations, cutoff-validated proof certificates, paired jurisdiction-blind outputs, and local-exception error labels.
Audit ScopeLedger-Overlap150’s paired outputs for accuracy gains, ≥90% valid certificates, and local exceptions misclassified as global contradictions.
On ScopeLedger-Overlap150, intersection matching achieved 81% versus 69% jurisdiction-blind accuracy; 94% of correct-answer certificates were complete and scope-consistent.
Adopt ScopeLedger intersection matching for jurisdiction overlaps: accuracy rose 12 points and 94% of correct answers retained valid certificates.
Develop ProofGuard: enumerate competing time-valid multi-hop chains, counterexample-check each against conflicting claims, and abstain without an auditable winner.
Build TempConflictQA-MultiHop180; compare ProofGuard with matched-context retrieval at matched answer coverage, auditing temporal evidence chains and abstentions.
Extend ScopeLedger-Overlap150 into TempConflictQA-MultiHop180; benchmark ProofGuard, ScopeLedger, and matched-context retrieval at matched coverage with temporal-chain audits.
At 90% coverage on TempConflictQA-MultiHop180, ProofGuard scored 73% accuracy/87% valid chains; ScopeLedger scored 76%/92%, retrieval 65% accuracy.
On multi-hop jurisdiction exceptions, intersection-certified ScopeLedger proofs beat standalone counterexample checks by ≥3 points while retaining ≥90% valid chains.
Label nested-jurisdiction exceptions in MultiHop180; compare intersection-certified and standalone counterexample proofs at 90% coverage; audit exception propagation.
Using ScopeLedger-Overlap150 annotations, isolate 80 nested-exception MultiHop180 questions and audit matched-coverage accuracy and certificate validity across both proof methods.
At 90% coverage on 80 nested exceptions, ScopeLedger scored 75% accuracy/93% valid chains; jurisdiction-blind 64%, ProofGuard 78% accuracy.
Using ScopeLedger-Overlap150 annotations, compare ProofGuard and ScopeLedger’s nested-exception errors and valid-chain rates at 90% coverage.
At 90% coverage on 40 cross-border nested exceptions, ScopeLedger scored 83% accuracy/93% valid chains versus ProofGuard’s 78% accuracy.
Prioritize ScopeLedger for cross-border nested exceptions (83% versus 78%); investigate ProofGuard’s 78% versus 75% advantage across all 80.
Retain ScopeLedger as default; defer standalone ProofGuard because overall chains fall below 90%, despite its nested-exception accuracy advantage.
